current_round.prompt:
Keep a per-Goal error from stopping workflow scheduling, and detect a live worker whose scheduling loop has stopped making progress.

The August field report is a hypothesis to reproduce, not proof that a specific stale-candidate error kills today's worker. Current execution already catches some task panics, but preparation runs in the scheduling path and scheduler_error suppresses admission until the pass ends. There is no scheduler-tick health evidence in the current runner. Round 1 retained unfinished failure-containment and watchdog changes without a candidate; its final log reports an unsuccessful agent exit and superseded attempt.

Contain preparation, Skill execution, result handling and failure-settlement errors at the owning Goal boundary. Ensure ended attempts release their local active entry and unrelated eligible work continues. Distinguish an authoritative failure, a superseded attempt and failure to persist evidence; retry transient persistence failures within a bound while rechecking authority. Never overwrite a newer Round or cancellation to make an old failure appear settled. Keep blocking Git, lock or settlement work from freezing the admission control path, without releasing capacity while owned work is still alive.

Publish runtime-local health tied to the actual worker incarnation and target, with ticks emitted by the scheduling loop itself. Use independent existing daemon supervision to detect stale ticks. Recover with bounded restart backoff only after safely stopping the old worker and its owned work, or report unhealthy with a concrete remedy if this cannot be proved. Keep daemon reachability and shutdown control available.

Use one shared health assessment in system status and refine next, distinguishing a stall from pause, missing required Plan/Implement Skills, scope or ordering blocks, long-running tasks and unavailable evidence. Keep worktree cleanup and deadline enforcement independently responsive. Share the latter and operation-recovery changes with Goal DR74050DA12C5442DF797B8AB6 instead of adding competing supervision.

Verify a superseded integration failure, preparation and settlement faults, and a task panic cannot stop the next eligible Goal entering Plan after capacity is available. Inject a non-ticking worker and verify detection plus safe recovery or unhealthy reporting. Test pause and legitimate waiting without false alarms, and confirm cleanup and deadline checks remain responsive without deleting retained work.

This is a recovery Round following the Skills review on 10 September 2026. Start from current main in a new managed Round worktree. Preserve Round 1, its plans, logs, branches, commits and uncommitted files; inspect and selectively reuse useful work instead of replaying the whole old attempt. Use the current Skills and docs/intent contracts, not archived Governance, Quality or Guidance configuration or the old fixed planning sequence. Refine owns workflow advancement and integration; human approval remains separate. Update only affected documentation and report focused verification with actual results.

goal.name: Keep workflow scheduling alive after Goal failures

result.summary: The plan addresses failure isolation, worker liveness, stalled admission, and independent maintenance while preserving authority and recovery safety.

checklist.description: Extend the existing per-Goal execution boundary to contain preparation, behavior, result-construction, and settlement failures or panics, ensuring each ended attempt delivers a completion outcome and releases its local active entry so unrelated eligible Goals continue.

Make settlement distinguish an authoritative failed or existing recovery outcome, a superseded attempt, and an unpersisted failure, preserving originating Round and revision evidence, retrying transient persistence failures within a bound with authority rechecked each time, and surfacing exhausted writes without overwriting newer Goal decisions or broadening automatic recovery policy.

Move potentially blocking Goal preparation and settlement out of the scheduling control path, bound or defer affected lock and Git waits, and account for in-flight preparation and live executions until they end so the next eligible Todo Goal can enter Plan within one poll interval after capacity becomes available.

Publish atomic runtime-local health tied to the exact worker incarnation and active target, with tick sequence advanced by the scheduler itself, last tick, last completed scheduling pass, active attempts, and failure context, using explicit startup and silence bounds that preserve liveness reporting during long-running Goals, pause, disabled automation, and app detachment.

Extend daemon-side runner supervision to detect missing or stale scheduler ticks independently of workflow execution and recover with bounded restart backoff only after confirming the old worker and its owned executions have stopped, retaining artifacts and reporting unhealthy whenever identity, termination, or replacement readiness cannot be established.

Expose one freshly evaluated workflow health assessment through shared system and process diagnostics so stalled scheduling makes daemon_healthy false while daemon reachability, shutdown control, and recovery supervision remain available.

Schedule agent hard-cap and idle enforcement independently through existing process supervision using recorded limits and activity evidence, preserving human-input and Toolbar timeout rules and containing individual inspection or termination failures.

Keep the existing worktree-cleanup worker independent of admission and worker-recovery waits, make its periodic supervision resilient to transient errors and bounded repository contention, and preserve pause behavior, cleanup eligibility, and retained evidence.

Extend the shared next-action service to surface locally eligible Todo Goals waiting beyond a defined admission threshold with free capacity and no active attempts, using shared scheduling eligibility and live process observations including interactive Goal sessions, and report the waiting count, last tick or unavailable evidence, and supported remediation while distinguishing policy blocks and unknown runtime evidence from all-quiet.

Keep failure containment, worker health, and maintenance changes within their existing shared responsibility boundaries and update only affected intent pages to describe settlement authority, liveness recovery, independent maintenance, and stalled-admission reporting.

result.summary: Strengthen Goal failure isolation and attempt-fenced settlement, detect and safely recover stalled workflow scheduling, expose delayed Todo admission through shared diagnostics, and keep agent timeout enforcement and worktree cleanup independently responsive so a live daemon cannot silently stop advancing work.

previous_rounds.prompt:
From: Ethan Jacobson <ethan.jacobson@insurity.com>
Subject: Refine daemon bug

Body:
## Summary
  The workflow runner-worker loop stops making progress after it fails to durably settle a
  stale-candidate integration, yet its OS process stays alive. Once wedged, the daemon admits
  no new work (Todo Goals never reach Plan), stops reaping agents past their hard cap, and
  stops cleaning worktrees �X indefinitely, until a manual daemon restart. Nothing detects or
  surfaces the dead loop: `refine next` reports "all-quiet" and `system status` reports
  daemon_healthy=true with running_workflow_processes=0.

  ## Field evidence (Refine 4.2.0, node bo2lnxnevo02-ethan, daemon port 8082)
  - Last log entry of ANY kind: 2026-08-18T21:50:00Z (category=workflow):
    "Goal failure was not durably settled (attempt superseded); original error:
     Candidate 11818bcf�K is stale: recorded base 2a4dccff�K is not <current>".
    Preceding lines show repeated "Candidate �K is stale" / "! [rejected] �K non-fast-forward"
    while integrating round branches during concurrent activity on merge_target_branch
    `insurity-claims`.
  - ~44h later: zero subsequent log lines. No "Workflow status changed" since 08-18T21:48.
  - A Goal created + started today sits in `todo` and is never admitted to `plan`.
  - system status: daemon_healthy=true, running_workflow_processes=0,
    parallel_run_cap=2 (capacity free). refine next: suggestion "all-quiet".
  - State-sync is healthy (sync_recovered 2026-08-18T13:48; `sync --preview` fast-forwards;
    origin push of refine/state succeeded today) �X so sync is NOT the blocker.
  - Collateral from the stalled loop: 3 agent sessions alive 21�V27h, far past
    agent_hard_cap_seconds=7200 and agent_idle_timeout_seconds=900, unreaped; 7 orphaned
    worktrees under .git/refine-worktrees not cleaned. This indicates the SAME loop that
    admits work also owns reaping/cleanup, and all of it stopped together.
  - Restarting the daemon respawns the worker and immediately resumes admission, reaping,
    and cleanup.

  ## Root-cause hypothesis (confirm in code)
  The "Goal failure was not durably settled (attempt superseded)" path �X reached when a
  candidate's recorded base is stale and the failure record is superseded by a concurrent
  attempt �X is not handled as a recoverable per-Goal outcome. Instead of logging the failure
  and continuing the loop to the next Goal, the worker's main loop exits or deadlocks (e.g.
  an error propagates out of the loop body, an await never completes, or a lock/worktree is
  left held). The supervisor keeps the process alive (so `system status` looks healthy) but
  the loop no longer ticks.

  Start in the workflow runner-worker entrypoint (`refine system runner-worker --kind
  workflow`) and the engine loop under src/application/workflow/engine/execution/. Find where
  "Goal failure was not durably settled (attempt superseded)" and the stale-candidate error
  ("Candidate �K is stale: recorded base �K") are produced, and trace what happens to the loop
  after that error �X specifically whether the error escapes the per-Goal iteration boundary.

  ## Required behavior
  1. A per-Goal failure �X including "attempt superseded" / stale-candidate / non-fast-forward
     push rejection �X must be caught at the per-Goal boundary, recorded durably (Goal ->
     failed or a recovery Round), and the worker loop MUST continue to the next Goal. No
     single-Goal integration failure may terminate or wedge the loop.
  2. Liveness detection: the worker must emit a periodic heartbeat/tick, and the daemon must
     detect a stalled loop (alive process, no progress/heartbeat within a bound) and either
     auto-restart the worker or mark itself unhealthy. system status must report a wedged
     worker as NOT healthy.
  3. Observability: when a Todo Goal has been waiting past a threshold with free capacity and
     no active runs, `refine next` must surface it (e.g. "workflow worker not advancing:
     last tick <ts>, N Goals stuck in todo") with a remediation command, instead of
     "all-quiet".
  4. Decouple or make independently resilient the periodic duties driven by this loop
     (admission, agent hard-cap/idle reaping, worktree cleanup) so one wedged concern does
     not silently stop the others.

  ## Reproduction
  1. Start a Goal whose implementation round races the merge_target_branch so its candidate
     goes stale on integration (recorded base no longer current), and arrange a concurrent
     attempt so the failure is "superseded" and cannot be durably settled.
  2. Observe the worker log the "attempt superseded" line and then stop ticking.
  3. Create + start another Goal; it stays in `todo` and is never admitted; refine next says
     "all-quiet"; running_workflow_processes stays 0; agents past hard cap go unreaped.
  4. Restart the daemon �� admission/reaping/cleanup resume. Confirms the loop, not the data,
     was the blocker.

  ## Acceptance criteria
  - A stale-candidate / superseded-attempt integration failure records the Goal outcome and
    the worker continues to the next Goal WITHOUT wedging; a follow-up Todo Goal is admitted
    to Plan within one poll interval.
  - A wedged/stalled worker loop is detected (heartbeat/tick watchdog) and auto-recovered or
    reported unhealthy in system status �X no manual restart required.
  - refine next surfaces a stuck-Todo-with-idle-worker condition instead of "all-quiet".
  - Reaper and worktree-cleanup keep running independent of an admission-path failure.
  - Regression tests (style of src/application/workflow/tests/ and
    src/infrastructure/process/supervisor/lifecycle/tests.rs): inject a superseded/stale
    candidate failure and assert the loop survives and the next Goal is admitted; assert the
    watchdog flags a non-ticking worker.

  ## Constraints
  - Preserve fail-closed safety for genuine content conflicts and never auto-merge contested
    Goal records; this fix is about loop survival, liveness detection, and surfacing �X not
    about weakening conflict handling.

skill.name: Plan
skill.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Inspect the repository and applicable context, resolve assumptions, consider alternatives and critique your proposed solution before finalizing it. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For a scoped finding recovery Round, focus the plan on the requested correction against the retained candidate. Do not change repository files. Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

## Intent and architecture

Applicability: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Model, Application, Infrastructure, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

checklist.description: Extract a cohesive per-Goal attempt runner covering preparation, Skill execution, result construction, and settlement, including panics; guarantee completion delivery with finished-handle fallback so an ended attempt cannot strand its active entry, while preserving current Event checks and workspace leases.

Return explicit authoritative failure, existing verified outcome, superseded attempt, and unpersisted-evidence outcomes; retry transient settlement failures at most three times with bounded lock acquisition and backoff, rereading Round, claim, node, and cancellation authority each time, and retain originating failure evidence without overwriting newer decisions.

Move blocking preparation, Git, and settlement work off admission control; bound or defer remaining promotion, Event, discovery, and lock work, and replace the pass-long scheduler_error latch with bounded retries while draining completions and ticking. Count preparation, execution, settlement, and still-live children against capacity, deduplicated with current Skill reservations and process observations.

Publish atomic runtime-local scheduler observations bound to port runtime, managed process identity, worker incarnation, node, and canonical target: tick sequence, tick time, completed admission-cycle time, active attempts, and failure context. Emit ticks from the scheduler itself at least every second, including pause and detachment; use a 30-second silence threshold and separately bounded startup progress.

Extend existing daemon supervision with one Application-owned recovery path using shared Infrastructure process controls: fence replacement launch, stop the exact old worker, rescan and confirm all owned process groups have exited, then accept a replacement only after its matching scheduler tick. Use bounded termination and restart backoff; retain unhealthy status and a supported remedy when identity, exit, or readiness cannot be proved.

Provide one freshly evaluated Application health assessment to system status, process diagnostics, and refine next; keep reachable unhealthy ports visible and separate lifecycle shutdown/readiness from workflow degradation. Report continuously eligible Todo work waiting over 30 seconds with free capacity, count, last tick, cause, and supported remedy; distinguish pause, disabled automation, required Skill availability and scope, ordering, retry delay, live tasks, and unavailable evidence.

Share deadline enforcement, confirmed process-group exit, and operation reconciliation with DR74050DA12C5442DF797B8AB6 through one daemon-maintenance interface and common health results. Reuse its implementation when available; preserve original recorded deadlines, Skill process coverage, human-input and Toolbar exceptions, live capacity, and operation evidence, with no competing reaper or recovery loop.

Keep cleanup supervision and deadline maintenance independently runnable during admission faults and worker recovery waits; contain individual inspection failures and defer repository contention. Preserve cleanup pause boundaries, retention delays, live-use checks, dirty-worktree protection, and exact ref-retirement fences.

Keep health policy and recovery orchestration in Application, runtime observation and termination mechanisms in Infrastructure, and surfaces thin; split changed mixed-responsibility files into cohesive modules. Update only affected workflow overview, consistency, execution-ownership, process, and CLI intent contracts.

Add deterministic regressions for real integration failure plus supersession, preparation/result/settlement faults and panics, exhausted writes, and transient scheduler errors alongside a long-running task; prove newer intent remains unchanged and the next independently eligible Goal enters Plan within one poll interval after safe capacity becomes available.

Exercise the actual worker and independent supervision path with a non-ticking process, replacement races, PID reuse, surviving descendants, termination failure, missing/corrupt health, target changes, and restart backoff; verify status and shutdown remain reachable, legitimate waiting causes no false stall, and cleanup/deadline maintenance progresses while retained artifacts survive.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: The August stale-candidate explanation is unproven on this candidate. Use fault-boundary analysis and a real integration regression; a synthetic error string alone does not reproduce the reported cause.

Reject wholesale Round 1 reuse: its unfinished attempt extraction omits current pending-Event checks and workspace leases, and its scheduler still retains the error latch. Selectively adapt useful boundary and test ideas against Round 2.

Reject timer-only heartbeats and Goal-completion deadlines as scheduler health. Measure actual scheduling iterations and completed admission cycles; maintain separate eligibility waiting windows that reset on pause, blocking conditions, or target changes.
Catching errors or terminating only the worker PID is insufficient. Completion must remain observable after settlement panic, and capacity or replacement launch must wait for proven owned-work exit.

Do not overlay degraded health onto today's lifecycle control flag: HTTP shutdown currently watches daemon_healthy, and running-status enumeration filters unhealthy ports. Separate these meanings before exposing scheduler degradation.

The companion deadline/operation Goal is currently in Plan without a candidate. Treat its shared maintenance and group-exit implementation as an explicit integration dependency; a stub or unverified hook cannot satisfy P7 or the combined acceptance tests.

plan.summary: Keep Goal failures isolated, detect stalled scheduling through independent supervision, and expose actionable health while preserving execution authority, capacity, and retained evidence.
